papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.why: Transformer architecture. Dense with exact terms (multi-head attention, positional encoding) and shares vocabulary with BERT — a good test of whether retrieval can separate two topically adjacent papers.

papers.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers
papers.why: Bidirectional pre-training. Overlaps heavily with the Transformer and re-ranking papers, so it stresses precision rather than recall.

papers.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
papers.why: The dense dual-encoder baseline. Directly comparable to ColBERT, and explicitly contrasts itself with BM25 — ideal for multi-document questions and for Experiment 003's core claim.

papers.title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search
papers.why: Late interaction. 'ColBERT' is a rare exact token that embeddings blur into generic BERT-similarity — the canonical case where lexical search wins and pure vector search fails.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP
papers.why: The RAG paper itself. Ties the corpus to the system under test and supplies questions about the architecture being evaluated.

papers.title: Passage Re-ranking with BERT
papers.why: Cross-encoder re-ranking — the technique Experiment 004 implements. Lets the system answer questions about its own reranker.

papers.title: BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-shot IR
papers.why: Retrieval evaluation methodology. Table-heavy, which also probes how badly the structure-blind chunker mangles tabular content (Experiment 002).

papers.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
papers.why: Position bias in long contexts. Directly relevant to why reranking order matters, not just which chunks are retrieved.
